findings.where: Nav bar lockup (arches + 'MMM INFRA') and the large hero mark, desktop and phone; the Palette section, which lists granite, cut, minium and lime only
findings.fault: The logo is shown in the wrong colours. In Mark's logo the wordmark is blue (#0070C0) and the arches are grey (#404040). Here both are drawn in the near-black 'cut' (#2A2925). The palette does not include the logo blue or grey as colours of its own, and it does not mark them as logo-only either. It says nothing about which version of the logo goes on the granite ground. The full-colour blue wordmark would likely fall below 3:1 on that ground, so it needs a version Mark has agreed to, not a quiet recolour.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo is meant to stay as it is (client value 7) and whose blue wordmark has gone from his own site without his say. The layout and animation rounds would also object: they would take a recoloured logo as the standard, when this round's job is to build the palette around the logo.

findings.where: Palette section, the LIME swatch beside MINIUM (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Lime is shown as a minium-red block with 'AA' on it. So the palette looks like it has two identical red swatches side by side, and lime's own colour appears only in two small letters. Every other swatch shows its colour as a block, so this one swatch works differently from the rest.
findings.who_objects: A designer in the next round reading the tile. At a glance they see one red twice and can't pick out lime as a colour, so the 'three colours' the note promises look like two colours plus a repeat.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel: the easing value 'cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.2, 1)' and the path 'docs/research/animation-length.md', desktop and phone
findings.fault: These two strings are set in the browser's default monospace (a Courier-like face). It is noticeably larger and heavier than the small Alegreya Sans around it, so a third, unchosen typeface breaks into a tile whose job is to fix a two-face type pair.
findings.who_objects: The next round's designers, who would read this face as part of the look. The house guardrail also objects, since it forbids the default font stack as a voice.

findings.where: Hero portrait stand-in label ('STAND-IN · PORTRAIT'), compared with the texture's 'STAND-IN' label
findings.fault: The portrait's label box doesn't sit inside the frame. It crosses the inner frame line and pushes right to the outer line, off-centre. Its text breaks so that the interpunct is left hanging at the end of the first line. The texture's stand-in label, which is the same kind of part, sits on one line and is neatly inset in its cell. Two matching labels are treated differently, and the one under the name looks badly placed.
findings.who_objects: Anyone looking at the first screen. The misplaced box sits right above Mark's name and reads as a careless build in a direction whose whole claim is precise, dressed-stone craftsmanship.

findings.where: Frames across the tile: the hero portrait frame (two thin lines), the article pull quote (heavy outer line plus thin inner line), the motion sketch panel and the LAY AGAIN button (one thin line)
findings.fault: The 'cut line' frame comes in three different weights for no clear reason. Most visibly, the portrait and the pull quote are both double frames but use different outer weights. The tile never states one frame rule for later work to follow.
findings.who_objects: Angélique and the layout round. With no single cut-line rule shown, each new framed part (a photo, a quote, a PDF box) will be guessed at, and the frames will drift further apart.

findings.where: Article specimen byline ('MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER 2024'); the motion table's column heads (ELEMENT, START, LENGTH, EASING); the stand-in labels
findings.fault: The type note says Cinzel capitals are for 'headings, the nav and the button only'. Yet the byline, the table heads and the small labels are also set in tracked Cinzel capitals. At small size the byline in particular reads as carved display lettering, not as metadata.
findings.who_objects: The layout round and Angélique, who get two rules that disagree. On every post a small run of capitals for a date and post number is harder to scan than the reading face would be.
